body:
Source: GitHub issue #1180 (bug). Verified on main @ 498a54d3.

PROBLEM. `classifyTrustRootTier` (packages/prosecute/lib/tier.mjs) ORs the `rails` of every ticket whose `completed !== true` over the changed files, and `loadTicketsForTier` (packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs) unions the base tip's tickets with the worktree's. So a bounded ticket that adds its own RED test as a rail, on the same branch as the change, tiers its own diff as trust-root: the recorder then demands a distinct-provider cross-model approve for a change that touches no trust-root surface. Reproduce: in a git repo whose base has one ticket T1 with no rails, a branch adds ticket T2 with rail `test/own/**` and a file `test/own/a.test.mjs`; `adlc-prosecute tier-check --base <base> --author-provider anthropic --ticket T2 --json` reports `trustRootTier: true` with reason `touches rails deny-path of ticket T2: test/own/**`. The CI rail-freeze gate (scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs, packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/rail-freeze.mjs) already takes the opposite rule: rails come from the base tip, and a PR may add a ticket without that ticket's rails applying to the PR itself.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. `classifyTrustRootTier({ changedFiles, tickets, ownTicket })` accepts an optional `ownTicket = { id: string, baseRails: string[] }`. A rail glob of the ticket whose `id === ownTicket.id` that is NOT in `ownTicket.baseRails` does not add a reason; it is listed once in the new return field `skippedOwnRails: string[]` (only globs that matched a changed file). The return value is `{ isTrustRootTier, reasons, skippedOwnRails }`.
2. Fail closed: an `ownTicket` without a non-blank string `id` or without a `baseRails` array skips nothing. Omitting `ownTicket` gives exactly today's `isTrustRootTier` and `reasons`, with `skippedOwnRails: []`.
3. Unchanged: rails already on the base (the ticket's own included), rails of every other ticket (also when another ticket declares the same glob), completed-ticket handling, and every non-rail surface class (trust-root files, CI control prefixes, enforcement and producer packages).
4. The bin derives `baseRails` from the BASE tip only (the canonical store and the in-repo `--dir` table at the base, same containment rule as `loadTicketsForTier`), never from HEAD, so a HEAD edit that narrows a ticket's rails cannot un-freeze a base rail. A base store or `--dir` table that exists but cannot be parsed exits 1.
5. The P5 recorder always passes its `--ticket` as `ownTicket`. `tier-check` passes it only when `--ticket` is given; without `--ticket` (the form CI runs) classification is unchanged. Both print one stderr line per skipped rail: `tier: skipped own new rail of ticket <id>: <glob> (not on base <base>)`. Every `tier-check --json` output carries `skippedOwnRails`.
6. Docs: the tier section of packages/prosecute/README.md and the bin's `--help` describe the rule, the stderr line and the JSON field.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 The four issue cases on the pure classifier: own new rail not tiered and listed in `skippedOwnRails`; own rail on the base tiered; another ticket's rail tiered; completed ticket not tiered. verify: `node --test packages/prosecute/test/tier-own-ticket.test.mjs`
- AC2 Fail-closed `ownTicket` shapes skip nothing, and omitting `ownTicket` reproduces the previous result on the positive-surface matrix. verify: `node --test packages/prosecute/test/tier-own-ticket.test.mjs`
- AC3 Process boundary over a real git repo: `tier-check --ticket T2` on the reproduction above exits 0 with `skippedOwnRails: ['test/own/**']` and the stderr line; without `--ticket` it still exits 2; `--ticket T1` still tiers; base rail `a` tiers while new rail `b` is skipped; a HEAD narrowing of base rails still tiers; the `--dir` table is read at the base; a malformed base `--dir` table exits 1. verify: `node --test packages/prosecute/test/tier-own-ticket-cli.test.mjs`
- AC4 Recorder: an own-new-rail change with a dry three-lens panel and no attestation exits 0 with no `p5-cross-model-missing`; the same change under another ticket exits 2. verify: `node --test packages/prosecute/test/tier-own-ticket-cli.test.mjs`
- AC5 Existing prosecute suite green. verify: `node --test packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs`
- AC6 Mutation gate green. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0

OUT OF SCOPE: packages/rails-guard (its CI gate already uses the base-tip rule), the cross-model-gate workflow, and the list of trust-root surfaces in tier.mjs.
title: prosecute: a ticket's own new rails do not tier its own change
